mainTopic: The essential wording of a גט and a גט שחרור, the dispute over "וְדֵן", and אביי's spelling rules for a גט
overview: The משנה finishes the essential wording of a גט with רבי יהודה's longer Aramaic sentence beginning "וְדֵן". It then gives the core wording of a גט שחרור: "הרי את בן חורין" or "הרי את לעצמך". The גמרא says it is obvious that 'free' wording does not divorce a wife, and 'permitted to any man' wording does not free a maidservant. It then asks whether "הרי את לעצמך" works for a wife, and רבינא proves it does with a קל וחומר from a slave. Next, a ברייתא about a slave sold to a non-Jew, explained by רב ששת, shows that "אין לי עסק בך" frees a slave. The גמרא explains that רבי יהודה and the רבנן disagree about ידים שאין מוכיחות, which is why רבי יהודה needs "וְדֵן". אביי then lists spelling rules so that no word in a גט can be misread. Finally, the גמרא asks whether we rule that "וְדֵן" is needed, rejects a proof from רבא's standard גט wording, and begins explaining the phrases "מיומא דנן" and "ולעלם". That explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's fuller wording for a גט
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says the גט must also contain a longer Aramaic sentence calling the document a scroll of divorce and stating that she may marry any man she wishes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says the גט must also say: "And this, which you shall have from me, is a scroll of divorce, a letter of leave, and a bill of dismissal, so you may go and marry any man you wish."
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is finishing its list of the essential words of a גט. רבי יהודה adds an extra sentence that names the document itself as a divorce document.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The basic wording permits her to marry any man. רבי יהודה wants the גט to also state clearly that this paper is the document of divorce. He uses three different names for it so that nothing is unclear.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
"And this, which you shall have from me,
phrases.notes: "This" points to the גט paper itself, which he is handing her.

phrases.english: is a scroll of divorce, and a letter of leave,
and a bill of dismissal;
to go and be married
to any man that you wish."

steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, a גט must also include a sentence naming the document as a divorce document and permitting her to marry any man.

steps.title: The core wording of a bill freeing a slave
steps.stepSummary: The essential words of a גט שחרור are "הרי את בן חורין" (you are free) or "הרי את לעצמך" (you are your own).
steps.simpleTranslation: The core of a bill freeing a slave is: "You are hereby free," or "You are hereby your own."
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now moves from a wife's גט to a slave's document of freedom and gives its essential words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each kind of document has its own key wording. A slave's release is written in the language of freedom and of owning oneself, not in the language of being permitted to marry. The phrase "הרי את לעצמך" will become the center of the גמרא's question.

keyTerms.meaning: The essential core wording of the document

steps.whyThisMatters: The גמרא later uses this exact line as a proof about a wife's גט.

phrases.english: The core of a bill freeing a slave is:
"You are hereby a free (woman) [person]";
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets, and the corrected wording uses the word in square brackets instead. Either way, it means 'free.'

phrases.english: "You are hereby your own."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the wording of a wife's גט to the wording of a slave's גט שחרור.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גט שחרור is valid with "הרי את בן חורין" or "הרי את לעצמך".

steps.title: Divorce wording and freedom wording cannot be swapped
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says it is obvious that "you are free" does nothing in a wife's גט, and "you are permitted to any man" does nothing in a maidservant's release.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is obvious: if he told his wife "You are hereby free," he said nothing. If he told his maidservant "You are hereby permitted to any man," he said nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by stating two obvious rules. Each kind of document must use its own wording. This sets up the harder question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A wife is not a slave, so 'free' wording does not end a marriage. A maidservant's problem is ownership, not marriage, so 'permitted to marry' wording does not free her. Because these cases are clear, the גמרא can now focus on the unclear phrase "לעצמך".

keyTerms.meaning: He said nothing at all (the document does not work)

phrases.english: GEMARA: It is obvious:
if he said to his wife:
"You are hereby a free woman,"
he has said nothing at all;
if he said to his maidservant:
"You are hereby permitted to any man,"
he has said nothing at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the משנה's two sets of wording by showing they cannot be swapped.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Freedom wording does not divorce a wife, and marriage-permission wording does not free a maidservant.

steps.title: Does "you are your own" divorce a wife?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether "הרי את לעצמך" said to a wife means she is completely free, or only that she keeps her own earnings.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he told his wife "You are hereby your own," what is the law? Does he mean she is completely her own, or only her own with regard to her work?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא asks about a phrase that could fit either kind of document. Is "לעצמך" good wording for a wife's גט?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A husband has a right to his wife's work and earnings. So "you are your own" might only give up that right, and then it would not be a divorce at all. Or it might mean full independence, and then it would be a valid גט.
steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether these words free a slave. The משנה already says they do. The question is only what they mean when said to a wife.

phrases.english: If he said to his wife:
"You are hereby your own," what is the law?
Is he telling her she is completely her own,
or is he telling her she is her own with regard to work?
phrases.notes: He means she would just keep the money she earns, which normally goes to her husband.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהּ לְאִשָּׁה: הֲרֵי אַתְּ לְעַצְמָךְ, מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the obvious cases, the גמרא asks about the unclear phrase taken from the slave's wording.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether "הרי את לעצמך" in a wife's גט means full release (a valid divorce) or only that she keeps her own earnings (not a divorce).

steps.title: רבינא's proof from the slave case
steps.stepSummary: רבינא points to the משנה: "לעצמך" frees a slave, whose body is owned. So it should certainly free a wife, whose body is not owned.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: Come and hear, for we learned in the משנה that the core of a bill freeing a slave is "You are hereby free" or "You are hereby your own." A slave's body is owned by his master, and still, when the master says "You are hereby your own," the slave gets full ownership of himself. A wife's body is not owned by her husband, so isn't it all the more so true for her?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא tries to answer the question with a proof. He quotes the משנה again and builds a קל וחומר from the slave to the wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה shows that "לעצמך" means full release for a slave, even though a slave is fully owned. A husband has a much smaller hold over his wife than a master has over a slave. So the same words should be enough to release her completely, and that would mean they form a valid גט.

keyTerms.meaning: His body is owned / he acquires his own body
Is it not all the more so? (a קל וחומר)

steps.whatToRemember: רבינא argues that "לעצמך" frees a slave, who is fully owned, so it should certainly release a wife, who is not owned.

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi:
Come and hear, for we learned in the mishna:
The core of a bill freeing a slave is:
"You are hereby a free (woman) [person]";
"You are hereby your own."
Now just as with a slave, whose body is owned by the master,
when he says to him, "You are hereby your own,"
the slave acquires his own body;
then with a wife, whose body is not owned by her husband,
is it not all the more so?!
phrases.notes: He means the words should certainly release her completely, so the גט works.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבִינָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי: תָּא שְׁמַע, דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer the question from step 4, using the משנה line from step 2.
steps.raayaObject: That "הרי את לעצמך" said to a wife means full release, so it is valid גט wording.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's wording for a גט שחרור ("הרי את לעצמך"), applied to a wife through a קל וחומר from a slave.

steps.title: Does "I have no business with you" free a slave?
steps.stepSummary: רבינא asks רב אשי whether a master who tells his slave "אין לי עסק בך" has freed him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא asked רב אשי: If a master said to his slave, "I have no business with you," what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא asks about a new phrase. Is "I have no business with you" strong enough to free a slave?
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already learned that "הרי את בן חורין" and "הרי את לעצמך" free a slave. This phrase is vaguer. It could mean full freedom, or it could just mean the master is stepping back for now.

keyTerms.meaning: I have no business with you

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi:
If he said to his slave:
"I have no business with you," what is the law?
phrases.notes: He means: is this enough to set the slave free?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ לְעַבְדּוֹ: ״אֵין לִי עֵסֶק בָּךְ״, מַהוּ?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the wife-related question about לעצמך to a new wording question about freeing a slave.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the phrase "אין לי עסק בך" is a valid wording for freeing a slave.

steps.title: A ברייתא about a slave sold to a non-Jew
steps.stepSummary: רב חנין brings a ברייתא. A slave sold to a non-Jew goes free but still needs a גט שחרור. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says that if the master wrote him "his document," that document itself is the release.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנין (some say רב חנין from מחוזא) said to רב אשי: Come and hear what a ברייתא teaches. If someone sells his slave to a non-Jew, the slave goes free, but he still needs a release document from his first master. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said: This is only when the master did not write the slave "his document." But if he wrote him "his document," that is his release.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חנין brings a ברייתא to try to answer רבינא's question. The key word is "אונו" (his document). The next step will explain what that document says.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says a special document written at the time of the sale can count as the slave's release. If that document turns out to say "I have no business with you," then the phrase works. The proof depends on the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: a document that frees a slave
his document (a special note written for the slave)
when is this rule said? (limits a rule)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב חָנִין לְרַב אָשֵׁי,
phrases.english: Rav Ḥanin said to Rav Ashi,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ רַב חָנִין מָחוֹזְנָאָה לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: and some say it was Rav Ḥanin from Meḥoza to Rav Ashi:
Come and hear, as it was taught in a baraita:
One who sells his slave to a gentile, the slave goes free,
but he needs a bill of release from his first master.
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said:
When is this said?
When he did not write "his document" for him,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל כָּתַב עָלָיו אוֹנוֹ – זֶהוּ שִׁחְרוּרוֹ.
phrases.english: but if he wrote "his document" for him, that is his release.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to answer רבינא's question.
steps.raayaObject: Whether "אין לי עסק בך" can free a slave.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's ruling that "אונו" counts as the slave's release.

steps.title: "His document" says: I have no business with you
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת explains that "אונו" is a note saying "When you run away from him, I have no business with you." So the phrase works for freeing a slave.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is "his document"? רב ששת said: The master writes to him, "When you run away from him, I have no business with you."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the unclear word "אונו." The explanation finishes the proof: the release document uses the exact phrase רבינא asked about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said this document counts as a release. רב ששת shows it says "אין לי עסק בך." So that phrase is a valid way to free a slave, and רבינא's question is answered.
steps.whatToRemember: "אין לי עסק בך" is a valid wording for freeing a slave. The proof is רב ששת's explanation of "אונו" in the ברייתא.

phrases.english: What is "his document"?
Rav Sheshet said: that he writes to him:
"When you run away from him,"
phrases.notes: "Him" is the non-Jew the slave was sold to.

phrases.english: "I have no business with you."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the key word in the ברייתא, which completes the proof.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: "אונו" says "אין לי עסק בך," and since it counts as a release, the phrase frees a slave.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: "אין לי עסק בך" works to free a slave.

steps.title: What is the root of רבי יהודה's dispute with the רבנן?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to רבי יהודה's extra sentence in the גט and asks what the two sides really disagree about.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says the גט must also say: "And this, which you shall have from me, is a scroll of divorce and a letter of leave." What do they disagree about?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה's dispute from step 1 and quotes רבי יהודה again. This sets up the question: what principle are they arguing about?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The quote is not new information. It is repeated to open a new discussion. The גמרא wants the reason behind the dispute, not just the ruling.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
"And this, which you shall have from me,
is a scroll of divorce and a letter of leave."
About what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the slave discussion and returns to the משנה's dispute about the גט.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The principle behind the dispute between רבי יהודה and the רבנן.

steps.title: The רבנן: unclear wording still works when the meaning is obvious
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן hold ידים שאין מוכיחות הויין ידים. So even without "ודן," it is clear he is divorcing her with this גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן hold: Unclear wording still counts as wording. Even if he did not write "And this" for her, it is obvious that he is divorcing her with this גט.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer by explaining the רבנן's view. רבי יהודה's view will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "You are permitted to any man" does not say which document divorces her. The רבנן say that does not matter, because the setting makes clear it is this גט. So the extra "ודן" sentence is not needed.

keyTerms.meaning: wording that does not clearly show its meaning

steps.confusionAlert: Here ידים does not mean "hands." It means wording or expressions that point to what someone means.
steps.whyThisMatters: ידים שאין מוכיחות is a famous principle across ש״ס, especially with נדרים and קידושין. Here it explains why the רבנן do not need רבי יהודה's extra sentence.

phrases.english: The Rabbis hold:
unclear expressions count as expressions,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא כְּתַב לָהּ ״וְדֵן״ –
phrases.english: and even though he did not write for her "And this,"
the matter is obvious
that he is divorcing her with this גט.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּנַן סָבְרִי: יָדַיִם שֶׁאֵין מוֹכִיחוֹת הָוְיָין יָדַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts answering the question by giving the רבנן's reasoning.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רבנן hold ידים שאין מוכיחות הויין ידים, so it is clear from the setting that this גט divorces her even without "ודן."

steps.title: Why רבי יהודה needs the word "וְדֵן"
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה holds that unclear hints do not work. So the גט must say "וְדֵן" to show the paper itself does the divorcing. Otherwise people will think he divorced her by speaking, and the paper is only proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה holds that unclear hints are not valid hints. The גט works only because he wrote "and this" for her, which makes it clear he is divorcing her with this גט. If he did not write "and this," people would say he divorced her by speaking, and the document is only evidence.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes answering the question from step 9 by giving רבי יהודה's side of the מחלוקת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן (step 10) said a hint that is not fully clear still works. רבי יהודה says it does not. So he needs "וְדֵן" to tie the divorce to the paper itself. Without it, people could think the husband's words did the divorcing and the גט is just a record.

keyTerms.meaning: Unclear hints. Words that only partly show what a person means.
"And this." The opening of the line in the גט that points to the document itself.

steps.whatToRemember: רבנן: unclear hints work, so "וְדֵן" is not needed. רבי יהודה: unclear hints do not work, so "וְדֵן" is needed to show the paper itself does the divorcing.
steps.confusionAlert: Both sides agree a גט must be the thing that divorces her. They only disagree about whether that must be spelled out in the words of the גט.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda holds:

phrases.aramaic: יָדַיִם שֶׁאֵין מוֹכִיחוֹת לָא הָוְיָין יָדַיִם,
phrases.english: unclear hints are not valid hints,
and the reason it works is that he wrote for her "and this"
so the matter is made clear
that he is divorcing her with this גט;
but if he did not write for her "and this"
people would say: he divorced her by speech,
and the document is just evidence.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second half of the answer begun in step 10, explaining רבי יהודה's side.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the רבנן and רבי יהודה really disagree about (step 9).
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהודה holds ידים שאין מוכיחות לא הויין ידים, so "וְדֵן" is needed to show the paper itself is the divorce.

steps.title: אביי: spell "וְדֵן" without a יוד
steps.stepSummary: אביי begins a list of spelling rules for a גט. The word "וְדֵן" must be written without a יוד, so it cannot be read as "וְדִין" (and a law).
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Someone who writes a גט should not write "וְדֵין" with a יוד, because it can mean "and a law." He should write "וְדֵן."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic. אביי starts giving rules about how to spell words in a גט so they cannot be misread.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Having just shown how important the word "וְדֵן" is, אביי warns that writing it with a יוד could change it into a different word, "וְדִין," meaning "and there is a law." Then the sentence would no longer clearly point to this paper.

keyTerms.meaning: "And a law" or "and judgment." The wrong reading to avoid.
Because it means, because it could be read as

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: הַאי מַאן דְּכָתֵב גִּיטָּא,
phrases.english: Abaye said: one who writes a גט,
should not write "וְדֵין" with a yod
because it means "and a law";
phrases.notes: With a יוד, the word can be read with a different vowel, so it changes from "and this" to "and a law."

phrases.english: rather, he should write "וְדֵן."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: הַאי מַאן דְּכָתֵב גִּיטָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the discussion of the word "וְדֵן," אביי opens a new set of spelling rules, starting with that same word.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Write "וְדֵן" without a יוד so it cannot be read as "וְדִין."

steps.title: אביי: spelling "אִגֶּרֶת" and "לִמְהָךְ" carefully
steps.stepSummary: אביי continues. "אִגֶּרֶת" (letter) is written without a יוד so it is not read as "roof." "לִמְהָךְ" (to go) must not be written with a יוד, and its ה must not look like a ח.
steps.simpleTranslation: He should not write "אִיגֶּרֶת" with a יוד, because it means a roof. He should write "אִגֶּרֶת." He should not write "לִימְהָךְ" with a יוד, because it can mean "for me from this." And he should not write "לִמְחָךְ" with a ח, because it means "like a joke."
steps.whatsHappening: אביי continues his list of words in the גט that could be misread because of a small spelling mistake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each rule protects a key word of the גט. An extra יוד can turn "letter" into "roof," or split "to go" into other words. A ה that looks like a ח turns "to go" into "to laugh," making the גט sound like a joke.

keyTerms.meaning: A letter. Part of the phrase "אִגֶּרֶת שִׁבּוּקִין" (letter of release) in the גט.
To go. She may go and marry whomever she wants.

phrases.english: And he should not write "אִיגֶּרֶת" with a yod
because it means a roof;
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the corrected wording, in square brackets, is "אִיגָּרָא," meaning a roof.

phrases.english: rather, he should write "אִגֶּרֶת" without a yod.
And he should not write "לִימְהָךְ" with a yod
because it means "for me from this";
phrases.notes: With a יוד, the one word can be read as two separate words, so it no longer means "to go."

phrases.english: and he should not write "לִמְחָךְ" with a ח
because it means "like a joke."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues אביי's list of spelling rules.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Write "אִגֶּרֶת" without a יוד, and write "לִמְהָךְ" with no יוד and with a clear ה, not a ח.

steps.title: אביי: three יודין, and long ווין
steps.stepSummary: The words "דִּיתִיהְוִייִין" and "דִּיתִיצְבִּייִין" need three יודין each, or they will refer to other women. The ו in "תֵּירוּכִין" and "שִׁבּוּקִין" must be long, or it looks like a יוד and changes the meaning.
steps.simpleTranslation: "דִּיתִיהְוִייִין" and "דִּיתִיצְבִּייִין" are written with three יודין each, because otherwise they mean "they will be" and "they will wish." And he should make the ו of "תֵּירוּכִין" long, and the ו of "שִׁבּוּקִין" long, because otherwise they mean "divorced women" and "released women."
steps.whatsHappening: אביי continues his list of spelling rules with two more warnings about יודין and ווין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With only two יודין, the words speak about "they" (other women) instead of "you" (this woman). A short ו can look like a יוד. Then words that describe the document as one that divorces and releases become words describing women who are divorced and released. Every key word must clearly speak about this woman and this document.

keyTerms.meaning: Divorce. From "סֵפֶר תֵּירוּכִין," a document of divorce.
Release. From "אִגֶּרֶת שִׁבּוּקִין," a letter of release.

steps.whatToRemember: אביי's rules all share one goal: every key word in a גט must be spelled so it can only be read the right way, speaking about this woman and this document.

phrases.english: "that you shall be" and "that you shall wish"
are written with three yods each;
because otherwise it means "they shall be" and "they shall wish."
And he should make long the vav of "divorce,"
and the vav of "release";
because otherwise it means "divorced women" and "released women."
phrases.notes: A short ו can look like a יוד, and with a יוד the words describe women rather than the document.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues אביי's list of spelling rules.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Write three יודין in "דִּיתִיהְוִייִין" and "דִּיתִיצְבִּייִין," and make the ו long in "תֵּירוּכִין" and "שִׁבּוּקִין."

steps.title: Last spelling rules: long ו in כדו, and how to write להתנסבא
steps.stepSummary: אביי adds two more spelling rules. The ו of "כדו" must be long. "To marry" must be written "להתנסבא", not "לאיתנסבא".
steps.simpleTranslation: The ו of "כדו" (now) should be written long, because otherwise it reads "וכדי" (for nothing). Do not write "לאיתנסבא", because it can be read as "she will not marry." Write "להתנסבא" instead.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי finishes his list of spelling rules for a גט with two more words that could be misread.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the ו in "כדו" is short, it looks like a י. Then the word means "for nothing" instead of "now." If "לאיתנסבא" has an א and a י, it can be split into "לא יתנסבא", meaning "she will not marry." That says the opposite of what a גט is meant to say, so it must be spelled with a ה.

keyTerms.meaning: Now (from the line "and now I have released you")
It means / it can be read as

steps.whatToRemember: אביי's whole list (steps 12–15) has one goal: no word in a גט may be misreadable as something that changes or reverses its meaning.

phrases.english: And he should make long the ו of "kadu" (now);
phrases.notes: This is the line in the גט that says "and now I have released and divorced you."

phrases.english: for otherwise it would mean "and for nothing."
And he should not write "le'itnasseva" (to marry),
because it can mean "she will not marry,"
rather, he should write "lehitnasseva."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues and closes אביי's list of spelling rules.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Write the ו of כדו long, and write להתנסבא with a ה, so neither word can be misread.

steps.title: Do we need the line "וְדֵן" in a גט?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the line "וְדֵן" is required in practice.
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: do we need to write "וְדֵן" (and this), or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the argument from steps 10–11 and asks how we rule in practice. This sets up the proof attempt in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן said "וְדֵן" is not needed, because unclear hints still work. רבי יהודה said it is needed. The question is which side the הלכה follows.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked before them (the scholars)
"And this": the line saying this paper itself is the גט

phrases.english: A question was asked before them:
Do we need "and this,"
or do we not need "and this"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the spelling rules and returns to the argument between רבי יהודה and the רבנן.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the הלכה requires the line "וְדֵן" in a גט.

steps.title: Proof from רבא's גט wording, which has no "וְדֵן"
steps.stepSummary: רבא's standard גט wording does not include "וְדֵן", so it seems "וְדֵן" is not needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבא set up this wording for גיטין: "We saw how so-and-so son of so-and-so released and divorced so-and-so his wife, who was his wife before this, from this day and forever." But he did not say "וְדֵן".
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to answer the question using the official גט wording that רבא set up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבא wrote out the standard text and left "וְדֵן" out, that suggests it is not required. That would mean we rule like the רבנן.

phrases.english: Come and hear,
for רבא set up this wording in bills of divorce:
"How so-and-so, son of so-and-so,
released and divorced so-and-so, his wife,
who was his wife before this,
from this day and forever."
But "and this" he did not say.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an answer to the question in step 16.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבא's fixed גט wording, which leaves out "וְדֵן".

steps.title: Rejection: רבא's wording leaves out other required lines too
steps.stepSummary: רבא did not list every required line of the גט, so leaving out "וְדֵן" proves nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: And by your logic, did רבא say all the lines? Rather, the others are needed even though he did not say them, and here too "וְדֵן" is needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof from רבא's wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's text is missing other lines that everyone agrees a גט needs. So his wording was only a partial outline, not the full גט. Since it is not complete, the missing "וְדֵן" may still be required.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your reasoning (turns the proof back on itself)

steps.whatToRemember: The proof from רבא fails because his wording was not a complete גט. So the question of "וְדֵן" is still open.
steps.confusionAlert: This step does not rule that "וְדֵן" is required. It only shows that רבא's wording cannot prove it is not required.

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning,
did he say all of them?
phrases.notes: He means all the other required lines of the גט, which רבא's wording also leaves out.

phrases.english: Rather, we need them anyway,
here too, we need it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 17.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from רבא's wording, not the רבנן's view itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבא's wording is incomplete; it leaves out other required lines, so leaving out "וְדֵן" proves nothing.

steps.title: Why the גט says "From this day"
steps.stepSummary: The phrase "מיומא דנן" is written so that we do not rely only on רבי יוסי's view that the date on a document already shows when it takes effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: The words "from this day" are there to exclude the view of רבי יוסי. He said the date written on a document already proves when it takes effect.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts explaining the wording of רבא's גט. It says the phrase "from this day" is written to cover the opinion that disagrees with רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יוסי, the date at the top of the גט already shows that it takes effect from that day, so "from this day" would be extra. The other opinion does not rely on the date alone. To be safe according to that opinion, רבא's wording spells it out clearly: from this day.

keyTerms.meaning: "From this day": the phrase in the גט saying when the divorce takes effect
"To exclude": the phrase is written so we do not rely only on a certain opinion
"The date of a document proves about it": the written date itself shows when the document takes effect

phrases.english: "From this day" —
is written to exclude the view of רבי יוסי,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר: זְמַנּוֹ שֶׁל שְׁטָר מוֹכִיחַ עָלָיו;
phrases.english: who said: the date of a document proves about it;
phrases.notes: He means the date written on the גט already shows when it takes effect, so by his view you would not need "from this day."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the question of "ודן" back to רבא's standard גט wording, and starts explaining it phrase by phrase.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The גט says "מיומא דנן" so that it works even according to those who hold, against רבי יוסי, that the date alone does not prove when the document takes effect.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that each phrase in the גט has a purpose. The wording is written to work according to all opinions.

steps.title: Introducing the phrase "And forever"
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא names the next phrase in רבא's wording, "ולעלם", and will explain it in the next line.
steps.simpleTranslation: The words "and forever"...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next explanation. It names the phrase "and forever" from the גט, and the reason for it comes in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line only quotes the next phrase of רבא's wording, the same way the גמרא did with "from this day." Nothing has been explained about it yet. The explanation follows right after.

keyTerms.meaning: "And forever": the next phrase in the גט wording, saying the divorce is permanent

phrases.english: "And forever" —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues going through רבא's גט wording, moving from "מיומא דנן" to the next phrase.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Setup line: it names "ולעלם" as the next phrase to be explained.
